stem.text: During a year, a country's national income in money terms increased by 3%, prices increased by 4%, and the total population increased by 1%.
What was the approximate change in real income per head?

points.text: Real income change ≈ money income change − price change = 3% − 4% = −1%. Real income per head ≈ real income change − population change = −1% − 1% = −2%

explanation.text: Converting money (nominal) national income to real national income requires subtracting the rate of inflation, since real income measures purchasing power rather than just the money value: 3% money growth minus 4% price growth gives approximately −1% real income growth. To get real income per head, the growth in population must also be subtracted, since the same real income is now shared among more people: −1% minus 1% population growth gives approximately −2%.

optionAnalysis.text: A decrease of 1% is the change in real national income (money income minus inflation) but stops short of also adjusting for population growth to get the per-head figure.
Subtracting both inflation (4%) and population growth (1%) from the 3% money income growth gives an approximate real income per head change of −2%.
An increase of 2% would require adding rather than subtracting the adjustments, which is the wrong direction for both inflation and population growth corrections.
An increase of 3% simply restates the money income growth figure with no adjustment at all for either inflation or population growth.

reasoningChain: Start with the given 3% growth in money (nominal) national income.
Subtract the inflation rate (4%) to convert to real national income growth: 3% − 4% = −1%.
Subtract the population growth rate (1%) to convert to a per-head (per-capita) figure: −1% − 1% = −2%.
This two-step adjustment (for both inflation and population) gives the approximate −2% change in real income per head.

inferredMistakes.text: Adjusting only for inflation and forgetting the second adjustment for population growth, stopping at −1% (option A) instead of continuing to −2%.
